---
title: "Demographics: Rural aging and population decline"
---

## Cambridge is caught in a storm buffeting rural school districts throughout New York

Population is declining in rural areas throughout New York. The main reasons are:

-  Declines in the number of births, a statewide trend
-  Out-migration of younger adults, leading to an aging population
-  Economic factors that make rural areas less attractive for new residents

[CLAUDE: The age chart is added at the end of the chapter, so the aging statement is now shown. Two bullets still go beyond the exhibits. "Out-migration of younger adults": the table shows net migration for all ages together, not by age. "Economic factors": nothing in the chapter shows these. The population project has migration by age if you want that shown.]

The chart below puts Cambridge's county (Washington County) alongside its
neighbors on both sides of the state line, reaching back to 1970. Each county's
population is shown **relative to its own 2010 population** (2010 = 100), so the
lines compare *trends*, not sizes. Washington County is the red line. Most of
these counties grew for decades; Washington County's population peaked in 2010
and has fallen about 6% since, while Saratoga County — the regional outlier —
has nearly doubled since 1970 and is still growing. The dashed lines are a
forecast: Washington County's population is projected to fall a further 7% by
2035.[^pop-chart]

[^pop-chart]: Values below 100 mean a county was smaller then than in 2010. Solid lines are history through 2024; dashed lines are the baseline forecast for 2025–2035 from the [popfc](https://github.com/donboyd5/popfc) population forecast project. New York counties: New York State Department of Labor intercensal estimates through 1999, then Census Bureau and Department of Labor estimates reconciled by popfc. Bennington (Vermont): Census Bureau intercensal estimates for 1970–1999 (from the National Bureau of Economic Research's consolidated file; census-year values are April 1 counts) and Population Estimates Program for 2000–2024. Bennington has no forecast because popfc covers New York only. The small upward steps in the Bennington line at 2000 and 2020 are census rebenchmarks: each census counted more residents than the prior estimates had shown.

[CLAUDE: You asked what counties were in the chart and whether to combine it with the forecast chart. It had six: Washington, Saratoga, Warren, Rensselaer, Bennington (VT) and Rutland (VT).
```{python}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
import os
import sys
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, os.getcwd())

import polars as pl
from plotnine import (
    aes,
    annotate,
    geom_line,
    geom_vline,
    ggplot,
    labs,
    scale_color_manual,
    scale_x_continuous,
    scale_y_continuous,
)
from great_tables import GT, loc, md, style

import comparisons as cc


def _find_repo_root() -> Path:
    cwd = Path.cwd()
    for base in [cwd, *cwd.parents][:5]:
        if (base / "data" / "crosswalks").is_dir():
            return base
    raise FileNotFoundError("Could not find repo root")


REPO_ROOT = _find_repo_root()
PROCESSED_DIR = REPO_ROOT / "data" / "processed"

pop = pl.read_parquet(PROCESSED_DIR / "demographics_county_pop.parquet")
components = pl.read_parquet(PROCESSED_DIR / "demographics_washington_components.parquet")
age = pl.read_parquet(PROCESSED_DIR / "demographics_washington_age.parquet")

#: Years shown. History ends at LAST_HISTORY; the forecast runs to LAST_FORECAST.
LAST_HISTORY, LAST_FORECAST = 2024, 2035
AGE_FIRST_YEAR = 1990

#: The counties charted, in legend order (the focus county first).
CHART_COUNTIES = ["Washington", "Saratoga", "Warren", "Rensselaer", "Bennington County"]

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Checks on the statements made in the text of this chapter. If the data
# change so that a statement is no longer true, the page fails to build.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def _series(name, period=None):
    rows = pop.filter(pl.col("geography") == name)
    if period:
        rows = rows.filter(pl.col("period") == period)
    return dict(zip(rows["year"], rows["population"]))


_wash, _sara = _series("Washington", "history"), _series("Saratoga", "history")
_wash_all = _series("Washington")
assert max(_wash, key=_wash.get) == 2010                     # peak year
assert max(_wash) == LAST_HISTORY                            # last year of history
assert round(100 * (_wash[2024] / _wash[2010] - 1)) == -6    # "about 6%"
assert 1.9 <= _sara[2024] / _sara[1970] < 2.0                # "nearly doubled"
assert _sara[2024] > _sara[2023]                             # "still growing"
# "projected to fall a further 7% by 2035"
assert round(100 * (_wash_all[LAST_FORECAST] / _wash_all[LAST_HISTORY] - 1)) == -7
# Bennington is the only charted county without a forecast.
assert [c for c in CHART_COUNTIES if not _series(c, "forecast")] == ["Bennington County"]


def _age(group, year):
    return age.filter((pl.col("age_group") == group) & (pl.col("year") == year))[
        "population"
    ].item()


_kids = {y: _age("5 to 17", y) for y in range(AGE_FIRST_YEAR, LAST_FORECAST + 1)}
_older = {y: _age("65 and over", y) for y in range(AGE_FIRST_YEAR, LAST_FORECAST + 1)}
# "about 11,000 aged 5 to 17 and about 7,800 aged 65 and over" in 1990
assert round(_kids[1990], -2) == 11_000 and round(_older[1990], -2) == 7_800
# "about 8,200 ... a quarter fewer" and "about 13,800 ... 77% more" in 2024
assert round(_kids[2024], -2) == 8_200 and round(_older[2024], -2) == 13_800
assert round(100 * (_kids[2024] / _kids[1990] - 1)) == -25
assert round(100 * (_older[2024] / _older[1990] - 1)) == 77
# "Since 2011 the county has had more residents aged 65 and over than aged 5 to 17"
assert min(y for y in _kids if _older[y] > _kids[y]) == 2011
assert all(_older[y] > _kids[y] for y in range(2011, LAST_FORECAST + 1))
# "the school-age group falls a further 10% by 2035"
assert round(100 * (_kids[LAST_FORECAST] / _kids[LAST_HISTORY] - 1)) == -10
# school-age share of all residents: "18% in 1990, 14% in 2024"
_total = lambda y: age.filter(pl.col("year") == y)["population"].sum()
assert round(100 * _kids[1990] / _total(1990)) == 18
assert round(100 * _kids[2024] / _total(2024)) == 14

#: Short, state-tagged labels for the chart legend (the Vermont county is tagged
#: so a reader sees the chart spans two states; New York is the default context).
COUNTY_LABEL: dict[str, str] = {
    "Washington": "Washington",
    "Warren": "Warren",
    "Saratoga": "Saratoga",
    "Rensselaer": "Rensselaer",
    "Bennington County": "Bennington (VT)",
}
COUNTY_PALETTE: dict[str, str] = {
    "Washington": "#C8102E",      # bold red — Cambridge's county, the focus
    "Warren": "#2C6E9B",
    "Saratoga": "#3F9C5A",
    "Rensselaer": "#8156A7",
    "Bennington County": "#E08214",
}
assert set(CHART_COUNTIES) == set(COUNTY_LABEL) == set(COUNTY_PALETTE)


def _indexed(df: pl.DataFrame, base_year: int) -> pl.DataFrame:
    """Add an ``index`` column = population / county's ``base_year`` value × 100."""
    base = (
        df.filter(pl.col("year") == base_year)
        .select("geoid", pl.col("population").alias("_base"))
    )
    return (
        df.join(base, on="geoid")
        .with_columns((pl.col("population") / pl.col("_base") * 100).alias("index"))
        .drop("_base")
        .with_columns(pl.col("geography").replace_strict(COUNTY_LABEL).alias("county"))
    )
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-pop-history
#| fig-cap: "Total population indexed to each county's 2010 population (=100), 1970–2035."
g = _indexed(
    pop.filter(pl.col("geography").is_in(CHART_COUNTIES))
    .filter(pl.col("year").is_between(1970, LAST_FORECAST)),
    base_year=2010,
)
order = [COUNTY_LABEL[c] for c in CHART_COUNTIES]

hist = g.filter(pl.col("year") <= LAST_HISTORY)
# Forecast segment, anchored at the last history point so the dashed line meets
# the solid one.
fc = pl.concat(
    [
        hist.filter(
            (pl.col("year") == LAST_HISTORY) & (pl.col("state") == "NY")
        ),
        g.filter(pl.col("period") == "forecast"),
    ]
)
washington = hist.filter(pl.col("geography") == "Washington")

(
    ggplot()
    + geom_line(hist, aes("year", "index", color="county"), size=1)
    + geom_line(fc, aes("year", "index", color="county"), linetype="dashed", size=1)
    + geom_line(washington, aes("year", "index", color="county"), size=2)
    + geom_vline(xintercept=LAST_HISTORY + 0.5, color="#999999", size=0.6)
    + annotate("text", x=LAST_HISTORY + 1, y=52, label="forecast →",
               ha="left", color="#666666", size=9)
    + scale_color_manual(values={COUNTY_LABEL[k]: v for k, v in COUNTY_PALETTE.items()},
                         limits=order, name="")
    + scale_x_continuous(breaks=list(range(1970, LAST_FORECAST + 1, 10)))
    + scale_y_continuous(limits=(50, 120), breaks=list(range(50, 121, 10)))
    + labs(
        x="", y="Population (2010 = 100)",
        title="Population by county, indexed to 2010",
        subtitle=f"1970–{LAST_FORECAST} (solid = history, dashed = forecast)",
    )
    + cc.theme_ccs()
)
```

The table below breaks Washington County's annual **components of change** into
its parts — births, deaths, and migration — so the decline can be traced to its
drivers. Negative migration means more people moved out than in.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-components
#| tbl-cap: "Washington County annual components of population change, 2021–2035. Births and deaths are counts; migration and total change are signed (negative = loss). Domestic and international migration are shown separately for 2021–2025 (Census Bureau); from 2026 on (forecast) only total net migration is projected, so the two split columns are blank."
tbl = (
    components
    .filter(pl.col("year") >= 2021)           # 2020 is a partial Census period (see note)
    .with_columns(
        pl.col("births").round(0).cast(pl.Int64),
        pl.col("deaths").round(0).cast(pl.Int64),
        pl.col("domestic_mig").round(0).cast(pl.Int64),
        pl.col("international_mig").round(0).cast(pl.Int64),
        pl.col("net_mig").round(0).cast(pl.Int64),
        pl.col("pop_change").round(0).cast(pl.Int64),
        pl.when(pl.col("period") == "forecast").then(pl.lit(" (fc)")).otherwise(pl.lit(""))
        .alias("tag"),
    )
    .with_columns((pl.col("year").cast(pl.Utf8) + pl.col("tag")).alias("year"))
    .drop("tag", "period")
)

mig_cols = ["domestic_mig", "international_mig", "net_mig", "pop_change"]

(
    GT(tbl, rowname_col="year")
    .tab_header(
        title="Washington County: components of population change",
        subtitle="Annual, 2021–2035 (signed; negative = loss)",
    )
    .tab_spanner(label="Migration", columns=["domestic_mig", "international_mig", "net_mig"])
    .cols_label(
        births="Births", deaths="Deaths",
        domestic_mig="Domestic", international_mig="International",
        net_mig="Net", pop_change="Total change",
    )
    .fmt_integer(columns=["births", "deaths"])
    .fmt_integer(columns=mig_cols, rows=pl.col("year").is_not_null())
    # Forecast years have no domestic/international split → show "—" not "None".
    .sub_missing(columns=["domestic_mig", "international_mig"], missing_text="—")
    .cols_align(columns=mig_cols, align="right")
    .tab_source_note(
        md(
            "**Source:** Washington County components from the "
            "[popfc](https://github.com/donboyd5/popfc) forecast "
            "project (history: U.S. Census Bureau Population Estimates Program, "
            "v2025 vintage, 2021–2025; forecast: popfc baseline cohort-component "
            "model, 2026–2035). **2020 is omitted** because the 2020 Census "
            "boundary makes that year a partial April–July period in the source. "
            "Domestic/international migration are not projected separately beyond "
            "2025, so only net migration is shown for forecast years."
        )
    )
)
```


## Fewer school-age residents, more older residents

The chart below shows two age groups in Washington County: residents aged 5 to
17, the school-age population, and residents aged 65 and over. In 1990 the
county had about 11,000 residents aged 5 to 17 and about 7,800 aged 65 and
over. By 2024 the school-age group was about 8,200, a quarter fewer, and the
older group was about 13,800, 77% more. Since 2011 the county has had more
residents aged 65 and over than aged 5 to 17. School-age residents were 18% of
the county's population in 1990 and 14% in 2024. In the forecast the school-age
group falls a further 10% by 2035.[^age-chart]

[^age-chart]: Solid lines are history through 2024; dashed lines are the baseline forecast for 2025–2035. Source: the [popfc](https://github.com/donboyd5/popfc) population forecast project, from population by single year of age: bridged-race estimates from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention for 1990–2019 and Census Bureau estimates for 2020–2024. The 2020 estimates are benchmarked to the 2020 census, which counted more children than earlier estimates had shown, so the school-age line steps up about 2% in 2020.

[CLAUDE: New chart and paragraph, added at your request. The paragraph states only what the chart shows; edit freely. I chose ages 5 to 17 and 65 and over because they are the two groups your title names. Working-age residents (18 to 64) fell from about 40,300 in 2010 to about 35,100 in 2024 and could be added as a third line.]

```{python}
#| label: fig-age-groups
#| fig-cap: "Washington County residents aged 5 to 17 and aged 65 and over, 1990–2035."
AGE_PALETTE = {"5 to 17": "#C8102E", "65 and over": "#2C6E9B"}
g = age.filter(
    pl.col("age_group").is_in(list(AGE_PALETTE))
    & pl.col("year").is_between(AGE_FIRST_YEAR, LAST_FORECAST)
).with_columns((pl.col("population") / 1000).alias("thousands"))

hist = g.filter(pl.col("period") == "history")
fc = pl.concat(
    [hist.filter(pl.col("year") == LAST_HISTORY), g.filter(pl.col("period") == "forecast")]
)

(
    ggplot()
    + geom_line(hist, aes("year", "thousands", color="age_group"), size=1.4)
    + geom_line(fc, aes("year", "thousands", color="age_group"), linetype="dashed", size=1.4)
    + geom_vline(xintercept=LAST_HISTORY + 0.5, color="#999999", size=0.6)
    + annotate("text", x=LAST_HISTORY + 1, y=0.6, label="forecast →",
               ha="left", color="#666666", size=9)
    + scale_color_manual(values=AGE_PALETTE, limits=list(AGE_PALETTE), name="")
    + scale_x_continuous(breaks=list(range(AGE_FIRST_YEAR, LAST_FORECAST + 1, 5)))
    + scale_y_continuous(limits=(0, 17), breaks=list(range(0, 17, 4)))
    + labs(
        x="", y="Residents (thousands)",
        title="Washington County: school-age and older residents",
        subtitle=f"{AGE_FIRST_YEAR}–{LAST_FORECAST} (solid = history, dashed = forecast)",
    )
    + cc.theme_ccs()
)
```

*Data sources:*

- **[popfc](https://github.com/donboyd5/popfc)** (Washington County, NY Population Forecast, sibling project) — NY county population history (NYSDOL intercensal estimates 1970–1999, reconciled Census PEP / NYSDOL series 2000–2024) and baseline forecast; Washington County components of change; Washington County population by age.
- **U.S. Census Bureau** — Bennington County (Vermont) history: legacy county intercensal estimates 1970–1999 (via NBER's consolidated file) and Population Estimates Program 2000–2024.
